page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-384 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the g4 server family. It features 384 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and is equipped with 1440.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its dense GPU configuration, which bundles eight NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs built on the Ada Lovelace architecture. This setup provides a combined total of 768 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. This massive graphics memory pool and parallel processing capability are designed to handle intensive rendering, visualization, and machine learning workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-384 represents a high-end hardware class optimized for resource density. By consolidating eight professional-grade GPUs and 384 dedicated vCPUs into a single virtual machine, it minimizes the overhead associated with multi-node cluster management. However, the absence of local storage means that users must provision external block storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff to consider during deployment.

This server configuration is engineered for highly demanding workloads such as large-scale 3D rendering, real-time simulation, high-fidelity virtual workstation hosting, and complex deep learning model training or inference. It is also suitable for data science pipelines that require massive parallel GPU acceleration alongside substantial system memory.
